title: Energy-aware performance portability with OpenMP dynamic variants
problem: Performance portability in HPC and embedded systems is often limited by power and thermal constraints. Systems need to balance performance with power caps and thermal limits.
motivation: Enable performance portability across diverse platforms while respecting power and thermal constraints through dynamic runtime variant selection.
method: The system extends OpenMP's variants mechanism (alternative optimized code paths you can write for different hardware conditions) with a runtime engine that decides which version to use as your program executes. It measures the power consumption and heat of each variant, then selects the one that best fits within current power budgets and temperature limits. Built into LLVM, the system runs lightweight monitoring code that collects these measurements and applies a balanced strategy that respects power caps, thermal headroom, and performance.
key_novelty: The first runtime system to automatically select between code variants during program execution based on real-time power and temperature measurements, while maintaining performance.
contributions: Energy-aware OpenMP dynamic variant selection runtime
Multi-criteria policy balancing power, thermal, and performance constraints
Validation on HPC and embedded platforms

metrics.edge_device_speedup: 39% execution time reduction (proactive vs hardware throttling)

limitations: No specific comparison with other dynamic specialization approaches. Limited detail on specific platforms tested.
primary_theme: Energy-Aware Dynamic Variant Selection for Performance Portability
